newsitem.title: USA: China soymeal imports higher in 1996/97 -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: China soymeal imports higher in 1996/97 -- USDA.

text.p: Soaring consumption for animal feeds will boost China's soymeal imports in 1996/97, USDA's Economic Research Service said Tuesday.
A smaller soybean harvest will slightly reduce Chinese soymeal production from the previous year, ERS said in its monthly oil crops outlook report.
"China has recently stepped up its imports of soybean meal, despite just completing its own soybean harvest," the report said.

It projected 1996/97 soymeal imports at 1.3 million tonnes, up from 1.1 million in 1995/96 and near zero prior to that. Once a significant exporter, China is now expected to export just 300,000 tonnes as domestic needs prevail, the report said.
Both the U.S. and Argentine soybean crush were projected higher in this month's report due to expanding Chinese meal demand.
